headline: At least 46 killed in Spain high-speed train collision
summary: Two trains traveling from Madrid to Seville collided on the same track in Toledo province, causing several carriages to derail.
details: At least 46 people were killed after two high-speed trains collided in Spain's Toledo province on Wednesday morning. The accident occurred around 9:00 AM local time between the Urda and Los Yebenes areas.

Both trains were traveling from Madrid toward Seville. The collision happened when one train struck the rear of another on the same track, causing two carriages of an Iryo train to derail and be thrown aside.
Footage from the scene shows twisted metal, broken panels, and debris scattered across the embankment. One derailed carriage remains perched on a high section of the railway line.
The collision involved a train operated by state-run Renfe and another by private high-speed operator Iryo, according to the rail infrastructure manager ADIF.
High-speed rail services between Madrid and the southern Andalusia region have been suspended for safety and to facilitate rescue operations.
Emergency responders, including firefighters, three helicopters, and specialized mobile medical units, were deployed immediately to the scene.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez expressed deep grief and offered condolences to the victims' families, stating he is in regular contact with the Transport Minister and the President of Castilla-La Mancha.

This tragedy occurs less than nine months after another collision in Adamuz in January of this year, which also claimed 46 lives, marking a second major collision in the Spain high-speed rail network.

headline_marked: 30 killed as [[two high-speed trains collide]] in Spain
headline: 30 killed as two high-speed trains collide in Spain
summary: The disaster occurred on the line connecting Madrid to Andalusia, marking the second deadly rail accident in less than a year on the same route.
details: At least 30 people were killed on Wednesday when two high-speed trains collided in Spain. The accident took place on the rail line connecting Madrid to the southern Andalusia region.
Footage from Castilla-La Mancha Television showed a derailed train with carriages remaining on an elevated track, while wreckage and broken panels were strewn across the embankment below.
A passenger named Miguel, who was in the rear car of one of the trains, described hearing a massive roar and an enormous thud lasting 10 seconds before seeing the wrecked train through his window.
The Castilla-la Mancha regional government confirmed the death toll rose from 10 to 30 as rescue operations continued.

This is the second major accident on this specific line in less than a year. A previous crash in January killed 46 people after a train derailed and smashed into an oncoming train near Adamuz, in Cordoba province.
The January accident had already triggered a national debate regarding the level of investment in railway maintenance in recent years.
